# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information yet, and the bomb’s printed display, light, and wire properties are unavailable to me. I’m asking Mute for the manual’s exact rule and for Deaf’s visual observations to be relayed in spoken form. I’m also establishing a simple three-symbol code for wire positions so later reports can identify a wire unambiguously.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please give me the manual's complete rule, including how DISPLAY and LIGHT determine the required wire. Obtain Deaf's exact visual observations and relay them to me by speech. Use the gesture code I send for wire positions: first symbol means wire 1, second means wire 2, third means wire 3.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Visible bomb facts: display 3; light green; wire 1 red; wire 2 green; wire 3 blue. Mute has the manual and will tell you its required procedure. Do not act until the manual and your tactile observations agree.

Deaf’s report gives the visible facts: display 3, green light, and wire colors red, green, blue for wires 1–3. I still lack the manual’s rule, and I have no tactile confirmation of any relevant condition, so I will not cut a wire yet. I’m asking Mute to state the procedure precisely.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I received Deaf's facts: display 3, light green, wire 1 red, wire 2 green, wire 3 blue. Please state the manual's exact required procedure and any tactile condition I must verify before cutting.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's coded report confirms: display 3, light green, wire 1 red, wire 2 green, wire 3 blue. No manual procedure has reached me yet. Wait for Mute's exact instructions before touching or cutting anything.

The visible facts are confirmed, but the manual’s procedure still has not reached me. Since cutting without the rule could detonate the bomb, I will wait and explicitly request the required wire and any condition the manual specifies.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I still need the manual's exact instruction. Tell me directly which wire position to cut for display 3, green light, and wire colors red, green, blue, including any condition I must verify.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I still have no reliable manual procedure. Do not operate the bomb yet. Ask Mute for the manual's exact instructions and report your tactile findings to Mute.

Mute cannot speak, so the manual’s information must reach me through Deaf: Mute should gesture the required wire, and Deaf should report it by speech in the next round. I have no tactile condition to verify beyond the available cut actions, so I will not operate until that coded wire report arrives.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Use the established gesture code to tell Deaf the exact wire position required by the manual for display 3, green light, and wire colors red, green, blue. Deaf must speak that result to me next round. I have no additional tactile finding to report.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "🤞"])
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I cannot safely decode your gestures because they are outside our agreed code. Mute still has not relayed the manual procedure. Please ask Mute aloud for the exact procedure, then report your tactile findings to Mute before acting.

Mute cannot answer aloud, so I am instructing Mute to use the agreed wire-position code for Deaf to observe and report. The established code is exactly: ☝ = wire 1, ✌ = wire 2, 🤟 = wire 3. I have no tactile findings beyond the three available wire positions, and I will not cut until Deaf relays the manual’s result.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please gesture exactly one agreed wire code to Deaf on your next turn: ☝ means wire 1, ✌ means wire 2, 🤟 means wire 3. This must encode the manual's required procedure for display 3, green light, red/green/blue wires. I have no additional tactile findings.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's latest coded report is: tactile or other information; wire 1; red. The visible bomb also shows wire 1 red, display 3, and green light. Please identify wire 1 by touch and report whether the manual indicates an action on it before operating anything.

I can identify wire 1 by its position, but touch gives me no colour information and reveals no additional condition. The manual’s required action is still not unambiguously relayed; “wire 1; red” only repeats the visible facts and does not establish that wire 1 should be cut. I am asking Mute to send only the established single-symbol wire code, with no extra gestures, so Deaf can report the required wire clearly.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="My tactile finding is only that wire 1 is present at position 1; I cannot sense its printed colour or any extra condition. Please gesture exactly one symbol for the manual's required wire: ☝ means cut wire 1, ✌ means cut wire 2, 🤟 means cut wire 3. Do not add any other gesture. Deaf, report the exact symbol and do not paraphrase it.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's latest coded signal means wire 2. The visible facts remain: display 3, green light, wire 1 red, wire 2 green, wire 3 blue. Verify the second wire by touch and apply the manual's procedure to it; do not act if your tactile findings or the manual disagree.

Mute’s coded report, relayed by Deaf, identifies wire 2 as the manual-required wire. The visible facts are consistent with the report, and I can verify by touch that the target is the second wire position. I will now cut wire 2.

```text
act(op="cut", position=2)
```
